papers.title: Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents
papers.problem: Agent builders treat MCP and command-line tools as equal, but the same actions behave differently in each.
papers.fix: Matched MCP and CLI interfaces gave different scores and costs, and the DART repair method added up to 9.0 points.
papers.practicalUseCase: Your tool format changes agent results, so test both formats before you commit to one.
papers.limitation: The test covered six models and three environments, so other agents may behave differently.

papers.title: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
papers.problem: Developers download small quantized models from public registries, and no registry tests whether the files actually work.
papers.fix: Seven of 305 official Ollama tags (2.3%) solved at most six of 164 coding tasks, though none were corrupted.
papers.practicalUseCase: A downloaded low-bit model can fail silently, so run a quick coding check before you use it.
papers.limitation: The audit covers code-capable tags only, and every failure was a low-bit model with at most four billion parameters.

papers.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
papers.problem: Teams that improve a reasoning model without a stronger teacher or labelled answers have few good options.
papers.fix: Making a weaker copy by pruning or quantization lifted average accuracy by 5.5 and 4.0 points.
papers.practicalUseCase: Small models can gain a lot with no extra labels, so try this before you pay for a bigger teacher.
papers.limitation: The gains come from math and coding tests, so other tasks may not improve the same way.

papers.title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
papers.problem: Image generators trained in fixed raster order cannot fill in, extend, or edit images unless you retrain them from scratch.
papers.fix: A short recipe taught pretrained models editing, beating MaskGIT on inpainting (FID 6.21 against 10.44) for 13-33% more compute.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can add editing to existing image models cheaply, so skip the costly retrain from scratch.
papers.limitation: Plain image generation gets slightly worse, with class-conditional FID rising by 1.2 to 1.9.

papers.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting
papers.problem: Nobody knew if AI agents can forecast company earnings per share as well as human analysts.
papers.fix: Three of six models matched analyst consensus, but their 80% intervals held the true value only 37-70% of the time.
papers.practicalUseCase: Agent forecasts look sure but miss often, so do not trust their stated confidence ranges.
papers.limitation: The test covers 149 firm-quarters from 86 US companies, so results may not hold elsewhere.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Few people knew how sustainability sukuk grew or what decides how big each issue is.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk, equity-based contracts, longer debt, and USD or Euro issues raised size; second party opinion costs cut it.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers get bigger sukuk with equity-based contracts and strong security, so plan those choices early.
papers.limitation: It shows links, not cause, and covers only 2012 to 2022.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic and conventional banks lacked clear evidence on which technology and governance factors drive their growth.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks, ICT adoption drove growth most, and high-tech exports helped only when paired with ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital investment pays off most for bank growth, so put money into ICT first, then governance.
papers.limitation: It covers 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so other regions may differ.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Muslim-majority countries still leave many people outside formal finance, even as Islamic finance expands.
papers.fix: In OIC countries, income, tertiary education, institutional quality, and internet access raised financial inclusion, unlike in OECD countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks in OIC countries reach more people when they build digital access and lift incomes, so start there.
papers.limitation: It covers 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in emerging markets set up sustainability committees, but nobody knew if those committees change environmental results.
papers.fix: Committees raised environmental scores in both bank types, but in Islamic banks they moved only overall and resource scores.
papers.practicalUseCase: A committee alone may only improve appearances at Islamic banks, so check for real products and innovations.
papers.limitation: It uses panel regressions, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant testing and peer comparison, but the global rate of impostor feelings was unclear.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among medical students worldwide, with large differences between studies and sampling methods.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you doubt your skills in a hard program, know that many peers feel the same.
papers.limitation: Study results varied a lot, so the pooled rate is a rough estimate.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students use generative AI heavily, but what drives their new ideas and research work was unclear.
papers.fix: Inner drive and outside rewards both raised innovative work, while long-unmet basic psychological needs sharply cut it.
papers.practicalUseCase: Protect your drive and basic needs first, because burnout kills new ideas faster than missing tools.
papers.limitation: It uses one-time self-reported surveys, so it cannot prove cause.
